items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: Benny Goodman, when Johnny Hammond (inaudible) Benny Goodman, (inaudible) Fletcher Henderson, Teddy Wilson (inaudible), he say he couldn't come back to these other people.

ctx.x: What -- I've heard it said that one of the things about process playing as a congo player is that some congo players are bottom players, and some congo players are top players. You know, some improvise melodically, but (inaudible) both.

What -- that's what I (inaudible) about Chano. The difference between Chano and everybody else, (inaudible) so many (inaudible) practically every place in the room (inaudible) play the same way. No, no, no, no. He always got to have something (inaudible), something that you don't expect. Well, he change this and that. Just the same thing happen to Dizzy.

Those people, they (inaudible) by themselves. They create (inaudible). And every time you (inaudible) the creator like that, you have conflict. Something they say, and I will (inaudible) into that again -- Benny Goodman and (inaudible) band or something (inaudible), but every one of those musicians, they go off key. They go off rhythm, and they make (inaudible).
